name: Onmyoji
description: Templates the Onmyoji pack needs. Wording is from the English Steam client, verified on a live game. Capture at the window size you will bot at. IMPORTANT: crop DISTINCTIVE content (words, banners, icons) — never a bare button. Onmyoji reuses one button chrome everywhere, and a crop that is mostly flat fill was measured matching a completely different button at 0.91.

templates.name: onmyoji_reward_confirm.png
templates.description: AFTER A FIGHT. The 'Tap to continue' line at the bottom of the post-battle screen (确定 / 点击继续), on a win and a loss alike. Both macros clear every result screen with it. It is a thin translucent line over changing backgrounds, so it scores over a wide band — measured 0.940 and 0.918 on raid overlays, 0.776 on a defeat screen, 0.737 on a battle-victory screen — which is why the macros ask for 0.70 rather than the usual 0.80.

templates.name: onmyoji_realmraid_attack.png
templates.description: ON DEMAND. The 'Attack' button in the popup you get after clicking a Realm Raid target. Not on the target list itself — select a target first.

templates.name: onmyoji_realmraid_refresh.png
templates.description: ON DEMAND. The 'Refresh' button at the bottom right of the Realm Raid target list. Also serves as the 'am I on the Individual list screen' marker, since it exists nowhere else.

templates.name: onmyoji_dialog_ok.png
templates.description: ON DEMAND. The OK button of the game's standard confirm scroll — raise one with Realm Raid → Refresh, which asks 'Raid log progress will be reset if you refresh. Continue?'. Verified on a live window at score 1.000. Without it the Realm Raid macro presses Refresh forever and never refreshes anything.

templates.name: onmyoji_realmraid_guild_progress.png
templates.description: ON DEMAND. The red 'Raid Progress' banner in the left panel of Realm Raid → Guild. The Guild list has no Refresh button, so this is how that macro knows it is on the right tab and, after a battle, that the list is back.

templates.name: onmyoji_level_up.png
templates.description: OPPORTUNISTIC. The shikigami LEVEL-UP popup — crop its BANNER or title text, NOT the OK button. Seeing this banner is what makes the macro look for something it can dismiss (the confirm scroll, then the 'Tap to continue' line); it never presses a position.

templates.name: onmyoji_defeat.png
templates.description: OPPORTUNISTIC. The battle DEFEAT screen — on the English client the banner reads 'Failed'. Crop the word, not the panel below it. Verified on a live loss at score 0.997. The macro clears this screen through its 'Tap to continue' line (reward_confirm, 0.78 there), never by position: the middle of this screen is a 'Get stronger via:' panel with three navigation buttons in it.

templates.name: onmyoji_captcha.png
templates.description: OPPORTUNISTIC — cannot be summoned; grab it the moment you ever see one. ANTI-BAN: the verification / CAPTCHA screen. Macros STOP on this instead of clicking through, so capture it carefully. Until it is captured, that guard does nothing.

templates.name: onmyoji_no_attempts.png
templates.description: OPPORTUNISTIC — appears only once the daily raid tickets are spent. The 'no attempts left / 次数已用完' state. Crop its message text. Stops Realm Raid (Individual); the Guild list counts separately, see guild_no_wins.

templates.name: onmyoji_guild_no_wins.png
templates.description: OPPORTUNISTIC — appears only once the daily guild raid wins are spent. Realm Raid → Guild counts a separate 'Win(s): n/n' in its left panel, not the ticket counter the Individual list uses, so it needs its own guard. Crop whatever the client shows when you press Attack with none left.

templates.name: onmyoji_inventory_full.png
templates.description: OPPORTUNISTIC — appears only when storage fills. The 'storage / inventory full' popup. Crop its message text. Stops the macro so you can clear space.

templates.name: onmyoji_reconnect_retry.png
templates.description: OPPORTUNISTIC — appears only on a network drop. The reconnect / network-error RETRY button, auto-clicked to recover. Include the surrounding message text so it is distinctive.

templates.name: onmyoji_wanted_quest_decline.png
templates.description: OPPORTUNISTIC — appears when another player invites you to a Wanted Quest, over whatever screen you are on. Crop the DECLINE / close / X button, with enough of the popup around it to be distinctive — NOT the accept button, and not the popup's title. The macro clicks exactly what this shows: capture the wrong button and it will accept every invitation instead of dismissing it, which takes the client somewhere the raid macros do not navigate back from. Until it is captured, an invitation that covers the list simply stalls the macro (it clicks nothing) and one that does not may get a grid click landing on it.
